contexts.text: These things concerning the creation, the garden of Eden, [and] down to the time of Abraham, Moses had from the descendants of the Most Ancient Church...
Moses himself had lost (the name Jehovah).

Preface. [2]. By Moses and Elijah (), who were speaking with the Lord, was represented the Word of the Old Testament, which was called also Moses and the Prophets; by Moses, his books, and also the historical ones... AC 5922:5.
The Lord was represented by Moses, etc.
Many of the Jews are introduced to Moses, etc.
The historicals of the Word are also called Moses...
To hear Moses and the Prophets () = to know the things in the Word, and to have faith in it; thus also to will them...
The Lord appeared to Moses in a human form adapted to his reception, which was external; namely, as a bearded old man sitting with him; as I have been instructed by the Angels.
Moses also married a wife from the gentiles.

The like was represented by Moses, when the skin of his face was radiant, as he descended from Mount Sinai... Moses represented the Word, which is called the Law... and therefore it is sometimes said the Law and the Prophets, and sometimes Moses and the Prophets. Illustrated. By the radiation of the skin of his face was represented the internal of the Word... His covering his face whenever he spoke with the people, represented that internal truth was covered over with them. AC 6752:9.
Moses () = the Word.
The Lord was represented by... many in the Word... By Moses was represented the Lord as to the Law or the historical Word.
In like manner when Moses died, the representative succeeded in Joshua, and afterwards in the judges, the kings, and so on.
In the supreme sense (in ) Moses represents the Lord as to the Law Divine, which is the Word; and, in the relative sense, truth Divine with the man of the Church.
She bare a son () = the Law Divine in its origin... because by her son is meant Moses, who represented the Lord as to the Law Divine, or the Word.

This transflux was the Divine Human before the Advent of the Lord, and was Jehovah Himself or the Lord in the Heavens. The Divine which transflowed through Heaven was the Divine truth, or the Divine Law, which Moses represented; and the Divine which transflows through Heaven is good. Hence it is evident whence it is that by she saw him, that he was good, is signified the apperception that it was through Heaven.
She hid him three months = the fulness of time in which it did not appear.
And she could no longer hide him = the time when it ought to appear.

As it had been provided that Moses should represent the Lord as to the Law Divine or the Word, in special as to the historical Word, it came to pass that when he was an infant he was placed in a coffer or little ark, but in a common one, because it was in its first rise.
Moses = the Law Divine; here, the Law Divine in its origin, because he was an infant.
Moses, who here is the child, represented the Law Divine, or truth Divine; thus truth from the Divine.

Moses, who here is the child, = the Law Divine in its origin; in the supreme sense, with the Lord, when He was making His Human to be the Law Divine; and, in the relative sense, with a man who is being regenerated, when he is being initiated into truth Divine.
Suckle him for me () = that it should insinuate into it good in agreement with the religiosity.
And the woman took the child, and suckled him = that good was insinuated into it by the Church.
The child grew = increase from good.
And she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter = the affection of scientifics.
As Moses represents the Lord as to the Law Divine, he could not have been brought to Pharaoh's daughter, and have been to her as a son, if the religiosity were signified by her, as before.
And he was to her for a son = that thence it had the first truths. Explained.

And she called his name Moses = the quality of the state then... (that is), the quality of the state of the Law Divine in its beginning with the Lord, and the quality of the state of truth Divine in the beginning with a man who is being regenerated.
There are two especially who represent the Lord as to the Word, namely, Moses and Elijah; Moses, the Lord as to the historical books...

The Law Divine, in a broad sense, signifies the whole Word; in a sense less broad, it signifies the historical Word; in a confined one, that which was written by Moses; and, in the most confined one, the ten precepts written upon tables of stone upon Mount Sinai. Moses represents the Law in the less wide, also in the confined, and also in the most confined sense. Fully illustrated.

As Moses represented the Law, he was allowed to enter to the Lord upon Mount Sinai; and not only to receive the tables of the Law there, but also to hear the statutes and judgments of the Law, and to command them to the people; and it is also said that therefore they were to believe on Moses to eternity ().
As by Moses was represented the Lord as to the historical Word... when He was transfigured, Moses... was seen talking with Him...

And she said, Because I have drawn him out of the waters = deliverance from falsities... In these words is contained the quality of the state which is signified by the name Moses; which quality, in the supreme sense, involves that in order to become the Law Divine as to the Human, the Lord delivered His Human from all the falsity which adhered to it from the mother, and this even until He became the Divine Law, that is, the Divine truth itself...
Moses grew () = ... increase in scientific truths.
He went out to his brethren = conjunction with the truths of the Church. Explained.
He saw their burdens = the apperception that they were being infested by falsities.
He smote the Egyptian () = that it destroyed the alienated Scientific.
He went out the second day () = conjunction again with the Church.

Who put thee for a man a prince and a judge over us? () = that it had not yet advanced into the truths of faith so far as to settle the dissidences within the Church... It has treated in the supreme sense concerning the beginnings of the Law Divine in the Lord's Human. It now treats concerning the progress of that Law; and in the internal sense it here treats concerning the progress of Divine truth with the man who is being regenerated. The progress is such that at first the man is able to discriminate between falsity and truth; for from the truth in which he is he can see what is false, because this is opposite; but he cannot at that first time settle [the dissidences] between the truths of faith within the Church. In order to be able to do this, he must make further progress; for a man is illustrated successively...
And Moses feared, and said, Surely the Word is known () = that it was among alienated scientifics, and not yet in truths, so as to be safe.

And Pharaoh heard this word, and sought to kill Moses () = that when the false Scientific perceived this it wanted to destroy the truth which is of the Law from the Divine... Moses = the Law Divine, and truth Divine, thus the truth which is of the Law Divine. It is said the truth which is of the Law Divine, and not the Law Divine, because as yet it is treating concerning the progress of the Law Divine in the Lord's Human.

And Moses fled from before Pharaoh = that it was separated from falsities... Moses = the truth which is of the Law from the Divine. Here begins the fifth state of the progression of the Law Divine in the Lord's Human; and, in the relative sense, of the progression of truth Divine with the man who is being regenerated; which is that of separation from falsities, and of adjunction with the truths of simple good. Next follows the sixth state, which is that of adjunction with good.
And he dwelt in the land of Midian = life among those who are in simple good.
And he dwelt near a well = study there in the Word.
Moses rose up and helped them () = aid from the truths which are of the Law from the Divine.
And he gave their flock to drink = that those who were in good were instructed thence.

An Egyptian man delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds () = because the scientific truth which is adjoined to the Church prevailed over the power of the doctrine of falsity from evil... The reason Moses is here called an Egyptian man, is that by Moses is here represented truth such as is with those who are in the truth of simple good.
And where is he? Wherefore have ye left this man? () = how, without this truth, could they be conjoined with the good of the Church.

The scientific truth which is here represented by Moses, is the truth of the External Church. This truth comes forth from the truth which is of the Law from the Divine, which also is Moses; and the truth which is of the Law from the Divine is the truth of the Internal Church. Unless external truth is from internal truth, it cannot be conjoined with good. Example(s).
Call him = that conjunction is to be effected.
And let him eat bread = confirmation in good.
And Moses willed to dwell with the man () = that they agreed together. Moses, here, = scientific truth...
He gave Zipporah his daughter to Moses = that he adjoined to it the good of his own Church... Moses = scientific truth.
For he said, I am a sojourner in a strange land () = that it had been instructed in truths in a Church not its own.

Moses was pasturing the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian () = that the Law from the Divine was instructing those who were in the truth of simple good... Moses = the Lord as to the Law Divine; but, in the beginning, as to the truth which is of the Law from the Divine; but here, as to the Law from the Divine. Thus may be named the degrees of progression in the Lord, before He was made, as to the human, the Law Divine itself.
Moses said () = perception from the Law from the Divine.
And He said, Moses, Moses, and he said, Behold me () = internal exhortation and hearing.
Put off thy shoes from off thy feet () = that sensuous things... were to be removed.
For the place on which thou standest is ground of holiness = that otherwise the Divine cannot enter.
And Moses covered his face () = that the interiors were protected.
Because he feared to look upon God = lest they should be injured by the presence of the Divine Itself.

And now go, I will send thee unto Pharaoh () = the Holy which proceeds from the Lord's Human, by which the infesting falsities would be dissipated. Moses, who was to go... = the Lord as to the Law Divine; thus as to the Human; for when the Lord was in the world He first made His Human Divine truth, which is the same as the Law Divine.
And Moses said unto God () = perception from the Divine, and humiliation... Moses = the Lord as to the Law Divine.
As the Lord is represented by Moses, and humiliation is here mentioned, something shall be said about the Lord's state of humiliation when He was in the world. Explained.
Who am I that I should go unto Pharaoh? = that it was not yet in such a state that it seemed to itself to be able to approach and remove the infesting falsities.
And He said, Because I will be with thee () = that the Divine [would be] in the Human. Moses = the Lord as to the Law Divine; thus as to the Human...
And Moses said unto God () = perception from the Divine.

And God said unto Moses () = the first instruction; (for) God says here to Moses, by whom is represented the Lord as to the Divine truth; and by Moses [it is said] to the people; thus by the Divine truth proceeding from the Divine Human of the Lord to those who are of the Spiritual Church...
Moses represents the Lord as to the Divine Law; that is, as to the Divine truth...
And thou shalt enter... to the king of Egypt () = communication with those who are in falsities... Moses = the Law from the Divine...

(In ) it treats concerning the Law Divine: that truth was adjoined to its good; and that thus the good had power to deliver, and to insinuate hope and faith. Moses represents the Law Divine as to good; and Aaron, as to truth.
Moses answered and said () = thought from the Law Divine... Moses represents the Lord as to the Law Divine. Thought from the Law Divine is [thought] from truth from the Divine.

The reason (Moses' rod) = the power of the Lord's Divine Human, is that by Moses is represented the Lord as to the Law Divine or the Word, which is the Divine truth proceeding from the Lord's Divine Human.
Moses fled from before it () = horror at the separated Sensuous.

And Jehovah said unto Moses () = Providence from the Divine... Moses represents the Lord as to truth Divine. Thus Providence from the Divine is predicated of the Lord as to the Human, when He was in the world.
That they may believe that Jehovah hath appeared to thee () = that they may have faith concerning the Lord's Divine Human.

(If they) will not hear thy voice () = if they do not show anything of obedience... Moses, whose voice they were to hear, represents the Lord as to the Divine Law; that is, as to the Divine truth; thus as to the Word, for Divine truth is there.
And Moses said unto Jehovah () = perception from the Divine... Moses represents the Lord as to the Divine Law in the Human when He was in the world.

I am not a man of words = that it has not speech... In the supreme sense it here treats concerning the Lord; for Moses represents the Lord as to the Law Divine; thus as to truth Divine. The truth which proceeds from the Divine immediately cannot be heard by anyone. (Continued. See Divine Truth.) AC 6983. AC 6985.

I will be with thy mouth, and will teach thee what thou shalt speak () = the Divine in each and all things which proceed from the Divine Human... As these things are said to Moses, by whom is represented the Lord as to the Law Divine in the Divine Human (this is the signification).

Send I pray by the hand Thou wilt send () = that the Divine truth proceeding from the Divine Human must be uttered mediately. Moses, who says these things, represents the Lord as to the Word; that is, as to Divine truth.
And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Moses () = clemency... because it is said to Moses, by whom is represented the Lord, when He was in the world, as to Divine truth.

Aaron... here = the doctrine of good and truth; and therefore it is said that he was for a mouth to Moses, and Moses was for a god to him. For by Moses is represented the Lord as to the Divine truth which proceeds from the Lord immediately... That truth which Moses here represents is the truth which cannot be heard or perceived by man... AC 7000. AC 7009. AC 7010.
Thou shalt speak unto him () = influx.

And thou shalt put words in his mouth = that the things which it utters proceed from the Divine Human. (For) Moses, who was to put words in Aaron's mouth, represents the Lord as to the Divine truth which proceeds from His Divine Human. (Continued. See Divine Truth.)
And I will be with thy mouth = that truth Divine must proceed through the Divine Human from the Divine Itself. Moses represents the Lord as to truth Divine. AC 7007.
And Moses went and returned () = what is continuous of the former life. Moses represents the Lord as to the Law or truth from the Divine.

When Moses was in Mount Horeb with Jehovah... he represented the Lord as to Divine truth; but now, when with Jethro... he represents the Lord as to truth from the Divine. Here... in the Word, in the internal sense, are described all the states of the Lord's life in the world, in respect to the way in which He then made His Human Divine... As the Lord thus put on the Divine successively, hence it is that He first made Himself truth from the Divine; afterwards Divine truth; and, at last, Divine good. These were the degrees of the Lord's glorification which are here... described.

And he said, Let me go, I pray, and return to my brethren who are in Egypt () = elevation to more interior and spiritual life in the Natural... For when going and returning are said of the Lord, who is represented by Moses, it means to be elevated to the Divine Esse or Jehovah who was in Him... AC 7020.
And Jehovah said unto Moses in Midian () = illustration and confirmation by the Divine in that state. Explained.
All the men are dead who sought thy soul = the removal of the falsities which endeavour to destroy the life of truth and good.
And Moses took his wife () = good adjoined. Moses represents the Lord as to the Law or truth from the Divine.
And his sons = the derivative truths.
And he returned into the land of Egypt = in the natural mind.
And Moses took the rod of God in his hand = that these things are from Divine power.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = perception from the Divine... (here), new perception.

And he was in the way in an inn () = the posterity from Jacob, that they were in externals without an internal... In these three verses it treats of the Spiritual Church, that it was to have been instituted with the descendants of Jacob; but that it could not be instituted with them, because they were in externals without an internal. On this account Moses does not here represent the Law or Word; but he represents that nation or posterity from Jacob whose leader he was to be; thus he represents also the worship of that nation... Hence it is that Moses is not named here, but still he is understood by he was in the way in an inn, and... Jehovah then met him, and sought to kill him; when yet He had before so expressly commanded that he should go and return into Egypt. AC 7043.

She said, For thou art a bridegroom of bloods to me () = that it was full of all violence and hostility against truth and good... In these three verses Moses represents that nation, and the representative of a Church with it; and Zipporah represents the representative Church. As Zipporah represents this Church, and Moses its external, she does not call him her husband, or man, but her bridegroom; for a bride can represent what is diverse... but not a wife...
And He desisted from him () = that it was permitted that they should represent.
(Jehovah said unto Aaron) Go to meet Moses () = that (the truth of doctrine) should be conjoined with the truth proceeding from the Divine immediately.

And he met him in the mount of God = conjunction in the good of love there. Explained... The truth which proceeds from the Divine immediately is called truth, but in itself it is good, because it proceeds from the Divine good; but it is the good to which all Divine truth has been united. It is called truth, because in Heaven it appears as light... The truth proceeding from the Divine immediately, enters into the will of man...
And kissed him = the affection of conjunction.

And Moses told Aaron all the words of Jehovah () = the influx of the truth which proceeds from the Divine of the Lord immediately, into the truth which proceeds mediately, and instruction in each thing of doctrine. Explained.
And Moses went, and Aaron () = the life of the conjunction of both; namely, of the truth proceeding immediately from the Divine of the Lord, and of the truth which proceeds mediately.

And afterwards came Moses and Aaron () = the Divine Law and the derivative doctrine... By the Divine Law which Moses represents is meant the Word such as it is in its internal sense; thus such as it is in the Heavens... Explained.

Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, draw away the people from their works? () = that their Divine Law and doctrine will not exempt them from grievous things. Moses represents the Lord as to the Divine Law.
They met Moses and Aaron () = thought concerning the Divine Law and the derivative doctrine.
And Moses returned unto Jehovah and said () = complaint from the Law Divine...
Why is this, Thou hast sent me? = when yet the Law proceeding from the Divine seems to say differently... Moses, who says these things concerning himself, = the Law from the Divine. AC 7167.
Moses (in ) represents the things which are of the Law Divine.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = instruction concerning the Law Divine. Explained.

That Moses... here represents the Law Divine such as it is with those who are of the Spiritual Church when they are in a state of infestations... is evident from the things which he said at the end of the preceding chapter...
And God spake unto Moses () = what is new, but continuous with what goes before.
The reason Jehovah is named in the historicals concerning Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, is that that Word was written by Moses, to whom the name Jehovah had been made known...
Moses (here) represents the Law Divine.
And Moses spake so unto the sons of Israel () = exhortation from the Law Divine to those who are of the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom.
And they did not listen to Moses = that they did not receive from faith and obedience. AC 7217, Explained. AC 7218.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying () = continuation.
And Moses spake unto Jehovah, saying () = the Law from the Divine, and the derivative thought.
AC 7225. And how shall Pharaoh listen to me, and I am uncircumcised in lips = that those who are in falsities will not receive, because to them I am impure.
The reason why Moses, because he was a stammerer, calls himself uncircumcised in lips, is on account of the internal sense...
And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron () = instruction anew from the Law Divine, and at the same time from doctrine.
She bare him Aaron and Moses () = that thence they have the doctrine of the Church and the Law from the Divine.

Aaron represents the External of the Spiritual Church, and Moses the Internal. The Internal of the Church is called the Law from the Divine... The Law from the Divine which is the Internal of the Church, is also the Word in the internal sense...

This is Aaron and Moses () = that from (charity and faith) were doctrine and the Law Divine with them... These, namely the Law Divine and doctrine, with those who are of the Spiritual Church, come forth principally from the Word, but still in application to the faith and charity which had existed with the establishers. Explained. AC 7239.

In that day Jehovah spake to Moses in the land of Egypt () = the state of the Church when command was given through the Law from the Divine to those who were of the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom, while still in propinquity to those in the Hells. AC 7241.
And Moses said before Jehovah () = thought concerning the Law Divine with those who are in falsities.

Behold, I am uncircumcised in lips = that the Law Divine is impure to those who are in falsities... But, in the historical sense, in which Moses as their head relates to the posterity from Jacob, and to that which is of the Church with them, uncircumcised in lips = that the Divine worship with that nation was such. Explained.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = instruction; here, how to proceed with those who are in falsities, and are infesting.
See, I have made thee a god to Pharaoh = the Law Divine, and its power over those who are in falsities.
From these things it may be seen in what sense Moses is called a god... namely, because Moses represented the Divine Law, which is Divine truth, and is called the Word.

Thou shalt speak all that I command thee () = the reception of the Divine influx... Moses, who was to speak, = the Divine truth... To speak = the mediate influx of Divine truth into doctrine... for the meaning is that Moses, who is the Divine truth, should speak what Jehovah commanded, to Aaron... thus to that which should communicate it. Explained... (For) Moses represents the truth which proceeds from the Divine immediately, and Aaron the truth which proceeds mediately.
And Moses was a son of eighty years () = the state and quality of the Law from the Divine. Explained.
And Jehovah said unto Moses and unto Aaron () = instruction. AC 7304.

And thou shalt say unto Aaron () = influx and communication; namely, of the Law Divine which Moses represents with the doctrine which Aaron represents... The reason the Law Divine, which Moses represents, should inflow into doctrine, which Aaron represents, is that the Law Divine is internal truth, and doctrine is external truth...
The Law Divine which is represented by Moses...
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = execution.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = new instruction. AC 7415.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = instruction... Moses represents the Law Divine, by means of which instruction from Jehovah is effected.
Say unto Aaron = the influx of the internal Law into the external Law. Explained. AC 7416.
And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron () = the presence of the Law Divine... Moses represents the internal Law; and Aaron, the external Law. AC 7451. AC 7587.
And Moses said unto Pharaoh () = answer. AC 7453. AC 7594. AC 7660. AC 7725. AC 7739.
Have honour over me = that truth Divine is to be trusted in... Moses represents the Law Divine; consequently, truth Divine.

And Moses and Aaron went out from before Pharaoh () = separation from those who have reasoned from mere falsities... Moses and Aaron represent the Law Divine; Moses, the internal Law, and Aaron the external Law. AC 7608.
And Moses cried unto Jehovah... = intercession.

And Jehovah did according to the word of Moses () = that it was so done, according to the word of the Lord; for that which Moses supplicated was indeed from the mouth of Moses, but still was from the Lord... AC 7470.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = instruction again.
Stand thou before Pharaoh = the appearance of the Divine to those who are in evils... because it was Moses who was to stand, who = truth from the Divine, by means of which the Divine appears.

And Moses said, Behold I go out from thee () = the removal of the appearance of truth Divine with them. Moses represents the Law Divine; thus also truth Divine. (Continued. See Divine Truth.) AC 7468.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = instruction anew. AC 7517.
Come to Pharaoh, and speak to him = the appearance of truth from the Divine with those who are infesting... (For) Moses, who was to (do this) represents truth from the Divine.
Internal truth is represented by Moses, and external by Aaron.
The reason Moses was to do this (which follows), and not Aaron, is that the truth which proceeds immediately from the Divine presents this effect with the evil.
Let Moses sprinkle them toward heaven () = that these falsities were shown to those in Heaven. AC 7528.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = instruction again as to what is to be done.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = command.
And Moses stretched out his rod unto heaven () = communication with Heaven.
By the hand of Moses () = by means of the Law from the Divine.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = command, namely, that which was to be carried to Pharaoh.
And Moses and Aaron came unto Pharaoh () = the presence of truth Divine... Moses and Aaron = truth Divine; Moses, internal; Aaron, external. AC 7656.
And He looked back, and went out from Pharaoh () = the privation of apperception, and separation... Moses, of whom (this) is said, represents truth from the Divine.
Moses and Aaron, who were driven out () represent truth Divine.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = instruction. Explained. AC 7709. AC 7765.
And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt () = the dominion of the power of truth Divine over the whole Natural of those who are infesting.
Hence it is that miracles were done by Moses; for Moses represents Divine truth. (Continued. See Divine Truth.)
And Pharaoh hastened to call Moses and Aaron () = fear then of truth from the Divine... Moses, internal; and Aaron, external. AC 7696.
And Moses stretched out his hand unto heaven () = the domination of truth Divine in Heaven.
And Pharaoh called unto Moses () = the presence of the Law Divine... By the presence of the Law Divine with those who are infesting, is meant that they perceived whence the plagues were coming...
These are words of anger against truth Divine, which is represented by Moses.
Moreover the man Moses was exceedingly great in the laud of Egypt () = respect now for truth Divine... in the mind of those who are infesting. AC 7788.

And after this I will go forth () = that truth Divine will depart... Moses [who says this] = truth Divine. These things signify that when those who have infested the upright are condemned, all truth Divine departs from them...

And he went forth from Pharaoh in the wrath of anger = the divulsion of the presence of truth Divine from those who are to be condemned... For when they begin to be averse to truth Divine, to fear it, and at last to feel horror at its presence, they tear themselves away from it...
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = information.

And Moses and Aaron did all these prodigies before Pharaoh () = that these vastations, and the consequent confirmations that they are in evil, had been effected by means of truth from the Divine; (for) Moses represents the truth which proceeds from the Divine immediately, and Aaron that which proceeds mediately... These prodigies were not done by Moses and Aaron, but by the Divine. But it is so said, because by Moses and Aaron is represented truth Divine; and the prodigies were done by the Divine by means of the truth proceeding from Him. For all things which are done by the Divine Itself are done by means of the truth proceeding from Him. Explained.
And Jehovah said unto Moses and unto Aaron () = information by means of truth Divine... Moses = the truth which proceeds immediately... AC 7994.

And Moses called all the elders of Israel () = the illustration of the understanding of those who are of the Spiritual Church by the influx and presence of truth Divine... Moses represents the Law Divine; thus the Word, and truth Divine.

(Pharaoh) called Moses and Aaron by night () = the afflux of truth from the Divine in that state... It is said truth from the Divine, and not truth Divine, because it is predicated of those who are in damnation.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying () = information from the Divine... by means of Divine truth. AC 8127, Explained.
And Moses said unto the people () = instruction by means of truth Divine.
In this prophetical () by Moses is meant the Lord.
Moses represents the Lord as to Divine truth. References. AC 8579.

And Moses said unto the people () = elevation from a state of despair by means of truth Divine... For all elevation in a state of temptations is effected by means of truth Divine, which... is meant by Moses.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = exhortation.
Why criest thou unto Me? = that there is no need of intercession.
Moses represents Divine truth.
And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea () = the dominion of the power of truth Divine over Hell. AC 8225.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = influx.
(They believed) in Jehovah, and in Moses His servant () = the Lord as to Divine good, and as to the Divine truth proceeding from Him and ministering.

Then sang Moses and the sons of Israel... () = a glorification by those who are of the Spiritual Church on account of deliverance... For Moses together with the people represents this Church; Moses, its head, because he also represents Divine truth.
Moses represents the truth of faith which proceeds from the Lord immediately; thus internal truth...
And Moses made Israel journey from the Sea Suph () = what is successive according to the order of truth Divine after they had passed through a region of Hell.

And the people murmured against Moses () = pain from the bitterness of the temptation... It is said against Moses, because it was against the Divine; for by Moses is represented Divine truth. References. AC 8404.
And Moses said unto Aaron () = the influx of the truth Divine proceeding from the Lord immediately, through the truth Divine which proceeds mediately.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying () = the truth which proceeds from the Divine of the Lord, in which there is the presence of the Lord.
And Moses said unto them () = information by means of truth from the Divine... Moses represents the truth which is of the Law from the Divine.
And Moses was angry upon them () = that they averted truth Divine from themselves.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = the appearance of the Divine obscured.
And Moses said unto Aaron () = influx... for Divine influx takes place through the truth which proceeds from the Lord immediately into the truth which proceeds mediately.
And Moses cried unto Jehovah () = interior lamentation, and intercession... by the Divine truth which is represented by Moses. Explained.
Yet a little, and they will stone me = that they are not far from offering violence to the truth from the Divine.

In the internal historical sense, in which it treats concerning the religiosity of the Israelitish nation, by Moses and Aaron is not represented truth Divine, but the religiosity of that nation whose leaders and heads they were... And therefore it was denounced against them that they should not lead the people into the Land of Canaan. Illustrated.

And Moses said unto Joshua () = the Divine influx into truth combating... because by Moses is represented Divine truth; that is, the truth which proceeds from the Lord immediately. This truth, being purely Divine, inflows into all the truths of faith, and causes them to be truths. AC 8601.
And Moses, Aaron, and Hur () = Divine truths in successive order. Moses represents the Divine truth proceeding immediately...
When Moses elevated his hand () = when the faith with those who were of the Spiritual Church looked towards the Lord. Moses represents truth Divine. Explained. AC 8606.

That stone supported Moses, and by Moses is represented truth in the first of order, or the truth Divine which proceeds from the Lord immediately. When the truth in the ultimate of order corresponds to this truth, then this truth is supported, for they then act as a one. Explained.
(In ) it treats of truths in successive order from the prime to the ultimate, and that they are ordinated by Divine good. Truth in the first degree is represented by Moses...
The father-in-law of Moses () = from which is Good conjoined with truth Divine.

All that God had done to Moses and to Israel His people = the perception of those things which had been done to those who are of the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom... For Moses together with the people represents this Kingdom; Moses as the head... Thus also Moses represents the Lord as to Divine truth; for the Spiritual Kingdom is from this.

And Jethro the father-in-law of Moses took Zipporah the wife of Moses () = good from the Divine conjoined with truth Divine... Truth Divine is represented by Moses. Zipporah, the wife of Moses, represents good Divine... AC 8656.

To Moses to the wilderness () = conjunction in the state before regeneration when there are temptations; (for) to come to Moses = the conjunction of the Divine good represented by Jethro with the Divine truth represented by Moses. AC 8660.
And Moses went forth to meet his father-in-law () = the application of truth Divine to Divine good.
And Moses told his father-in-law... () = perception then from truth Divine.

And Moses sat to judge the people () = the disposing of truth Divine with those of the Spiritual Church in the state before it is from good. Moses represents the truth Divine proceeding from the Lord immediately.
Immediate influx is represented by Moses alone having judged the people...

And the people stood over Moses = obedience then from truth Divine... To stand over Moses = to consult truth Divine, and to await an answer from it, and to do according to it... By these things is described the first state in which the man who is being regenerated is led by means of truth from the Lord...

Wherefore sittest thou alone? () = that it was without the influx of truth from good from any other source; (because) it is said of the truth Divine proceeding from the Lord immediately, which is represented by Moses; (and thus) = influx from him alone...
Explained.
And Moses said to his father-in-law () = what is reciprocal which is in the reply... because by Moses is represented Divine truth conjoined with and united to Divine good...
Because the people come to me to inquire of God = that they will and act from no other source than the fact that the Word has so said. Moses represents truth Divine; thus the Word.
They come to me, and I judge between a man and his companion () = that they are then disposed from revealed truth. Explained.
The word which thou doest is not good () = that a change must be made.

In wasting away thou wilt waste away, both thou, and also this people that is with thee () = that thus the truth which has been inseminated will perish... By Moses is meant truth from the Divine; and by the people, those who are receiving it. AC 8700, Explained. AC 8701, Explained.

I will consult for thee, and God shall be with thee () = that it is from the Divine... [The expression] from the Divine, which is signified by God shall be with thee, regards the Divine truth which is represented by Moses.
Be thou for the people with God = the truth proceeding from the Lord immediately...
And bring thou the words unto God = mediation and intercession... (These) are of Divine truth, because this is most nearly with Divine good, which is the Lord Himself... AC 8729.
And thou shalt teach them statutes and laws () = that from the immediate truth from the Lord are the external and internal goods and truths of the Church... AC 8707. AC 8708.
And look thou out of all the people () = the choice of subservient truths... here, truths subservient to the truth immediately from the Divine, which is represented by Moses.
Princes... here, = truths from good, because these princes were to be under Moses, by whom is represented truth Divine proceeding from Divine good; that is, from the Lord.
Every great word they shall bring to thee () = that everything is from the truth immediately from the Divine. Explained.
Devolve from upon thee, and let them bear it with thee = thus functions and offices for them. Explained.

And Moses hearkened to the voice of his father-in-law... () = the effect... By Moses is represented the Divine truth which proceeds from Divine good; (and which) acts nothing from itself; but from the Divine good. Explained.
And Moses sent away his father-in-law () = the accommodated state of truth Divine. Explained.

And Moses ascended unto God () = the truth from the Divine which is below Heaven conjoining itself with the Divine truth which is in Heaven. Moses, here, represents the truth from the Divine which is below Heaven, for the reason that he now represents the sons of Israel as their head; thus those who are of the Spiritual Church, who as yet are not in Heaven, because not yet in good formed by truths...
Moses () represents truth from the Divine conjoined with the truth Divine in Heaven, which mediates.
And Jehovah said unto Moses () = the influx of the Divine by means of truth from the Divine concerning the revelation.
Behold I come unto thee in the density of a cloud = that this shall be done in a form the most natural... By Moses is represented the truth from the Divine which is of the Spiritual Church.

The representation of Moses now is the truth from the Divine which is below Heaven... The truth from the Divine, which is represented by Moses, is the mediating [agent] of the Divine with those who are of the Church... and therefore also by Moses is represented the truth from the Divine below Heaven conjoined with the truth Divine in Heaven; and this on account of the mediation.
Those who are intermediate between the Celestial Kingdom and the Spiritual Kingdom... are represented by Moses, and also by Aaron, to whom it was granted to ascend into the mountain. Explained.
And Moses descended from the mountain to the people () = application and preparation by means of truth from the Divine for the receiving of truths in good.

By Moses in this and the following chapters is represented the truth from the Divine below Heaven conjoined with the truth Divine in Heaven, and hence mediating between the Divine in Heaven and the good in which truths are to be implanted, which is of the Spiritual Church; thus mediating between the Lord and the people.
And Moses made the people go forth to meet God... () = the power of truth from the Divine to prepare them to receive the Divine.
Moses spake, and God answered him in a voice () = by means of influx of truth from the Divine, in which was the Divine Itself.
And Jehovah called Moses to the head of the mountain, and Moses ascended () = the conjunction of truth from the Divine there.
And Moses said unto Jehovah () = the thought of truth from the Divine... For it is the truth with a man which thinks. Explained.
And ascend, thou and Aaron () = conjunction with truth from the Divine, internal and external.
And Moses descended unto the people () = the influx of the Divine through truth from the Divine.

Speak thou with us () = the reception of truth in an accommodated form, which they would then obey... Moses, who was to speak, represents the truth from the Divine below Heaven conjoined with the truth Divine in Heaven; thus mediating between the Lord and the people. Hence it is that Moses, here, = truth in an accommodated form. (Continued. See Divine Truth.) AC 8921.

And Moses came near unto the thick darkness where God was () = the conjunction still of the truth of spiritual good with truth Divine. Moses represents the truth Divine below Heaven conjoined with the truth Divine in Heaven, and consequently mediating; thus the truth of spiritual good; for this is truth Divine below Heaven, in which is the Spiritual Church... This truth Moses represents as the head of that Church.
The other reason why Moses is said to have entered into the thick darkness, when he came near to God, is that Moses as their leader represented the Israelitish and Jewish people...
And He said unto Moses () = that which concerns the Word in general. Moses represents the Word.
In the Word there are a number who represent the Lord as to truth Divine, or as to the Word; but among these the chief ones are Moses, Elijah, Elisha, and John the Baptist.
Moses (at the transfiguration) = the historical Word.
(Ascend to Jehovah) thou and Aaron = (the conjunction with the Lord of the) Word in the internal and the external sense.
And Moses, he alone, shall come near unto Jehovah () = the conjunction and presence of the Lord through the Word in general... Moses represents the Word in general.
And Moses came and announced to the people () = illustration and information by the Lord through the Divine truth which is from Himself. Explained.

And Moses wrote all the words of Jehovah () = impression then on the life. Moses represents the Lord as to the Word. (Thus by the above words) are signified truths Divine impressed on the life by the Lord. Explained.
That the books of Moses are called the Book of the Covenant.
There ascended Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, () = the Word in the internal and external sense, and the doctrine from both.

And Jehovah said unto Moses () = instruction by the Lord for those who are in the external sense... Moses represents that which mediates between the Lord and the people; thus the Word as to its external Holy; for this is what mediates. That this is what Moses now begins to represent, is evident from the series of things which follow; for that people were in the external of the Word... They who are such cannot possibly have any communication with the Lord... except through an intermediate.
On this account that people was no longer called the people of Jehovah, but the people of Moses. Illustrated.
The reason Moses before represented the Word in general; that is, as to both its internal and its external sense, was that it there treated of the promulgation of the Law...
Ascend thou unto Me in the mountain = the Lord's presence with them through the intermediate... Because Moses now represents the people as their head, and thus as one who mediates.

And Moses rose up, and Joshua his minister () = the Word and the representative. Moses represents that which mediates between the Lord and the people who are in the external sense of the Word separated from the internal; thus also the Word; as shown above in AC 9414... The representative... ministers, so that the externals of the Word and of worship may be presented before the Lord through the intermediate, which was Moses. (Explained under Holy.)
And Moses ascended unto the mountain of God = towards Heaven.
For when Moses ascended unto the mountain, he represented the external Holy of the Word, which is intermediate... between its internal Holy and the representative which is of the external sense.

And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud () = the Word in the external sense; (for) Moses represents the Word; here, the Word in the external sense, because it is said that he entered into the midst of the cloud... That Moses remained in the extreme (or outermost) of the mountain six days, and on the seventh day was called and entered into the cloud, and ascended unto the mountain, took place for the reason that he might represent the intermediate... between the people and the Lord... The degrees of ascent from the people to the Lord are thus described. And when at last he came into the mountain, he then for the first time represented the external Holy of the Word, which is what mediates... but still he was admitted no further than to the first threshold of Heaven, where the external Holy of the Word ceases. How far he was admitted, has been shown me representatively by means of a Spirit, who as to the upper part of his face as far as the chin was seen in the light of Heaven; but as to the lower part, from the chin, and as to the whole body, was in a cloud. Hence it was evident how much of the external Holy, which mediates, he represented.

The six days during which Moses remained in the extreme of the mountain, signified a state of truth; and the seventh, in which he ascended unto the mountain, a state of good. The reason is that there are like degrees of ascent from the world to Heaven with those who are being regenerated by the Lord... Such elevation or ascent was also represented by Moses when he put on the representation of the external Holy which mediates; for the external Holy of the Word is the entrance to a state of good; thus to Heaven.
And Moses was in the mountain forty days and forty nights = what is plenary as to information and influx.

That forty also = what is plenary as to influx, is because from this time Moses begins to represent the external Holy of the Word, which is what mediates between the Lord and the people; and mediation is effected by means of influx through that Holy into the representative in which the people were.
Moses, to whom the Testimony was given, represents the Lord as to Divine truth.
Cause thou to approach unto thee Aaron thy brother () = the conjunction of Divine truth with Divine good in the Lord's Divine Human. Moses represents the Lord as to Divine truth.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying () = illustration through the Word by the Lord... By Moses is represented the Word. AC 10354. AC 10355.
By Moses is represented the Lord as to the Word.
And He gave unto Moses in His finishing to speak with him the two tables of the Testimony () = the conjunction of the Lord with man through the Word. Moses represents the Word.
And the people saw that Moses delayed to descend from the mountain () = the Israelitish nation when they did not apperceive in the Word anything from Heaven... Moses represents the Word.

Because this Moses, that man who made us ascend from the land of Egypt, we know not what has become of him () = that it is altogether unknown what Divine truth there is in the Word other than that which elevates man from what is external into what is internal, and makes the Church. Moses represents the Word; thus Divine truth.
And I will make thee into a great nation () = the Word elsewhere, that it is good and excellent. Moses represents the Word.
And Moses deprecated the faces of Jehovah () = that the Lord from mercy remembered. Moses represents the Word.
And Moses looked back, and descended from the mountain () = the Word let down from Heaven.
Moses represented the Word, which is the Divine truth itself from the Lord, and therefore the tables were in his hand, as a badge of this representation. AC 10690.

And the anger of Moses was kindled () = the turning away of that nation from the internal of the Word, of the Church, and of worship... because by Moses is represented the Word or Divine truth which is from the Lord; or, what is the same, the Lord as to Divine truth.

And Moses said unto Aaron () = perception from the Internal concerning such an External... Moses represents the Word; here, its internal... The reason Moses here = the Internal, is that he is speaking to Aaron... AC 10471. AC 10479.
And Moses stood in the gate of the camp () = where is the opening to Hell. Moses represents the Internal... (which) cannot enter into Hell...
And if not, blot me I pray out of Thy book which Thou hast written () = that the internal of the Word, of the Church, and of worship will not perish. Explained.
When Moses went forth to the camp... (); Moses here represents the Word. AC 10550. AC 10551. AC 10554.
When Moses has returned to the camp, he no longer represents the Word, but the head of the Israelitish nation...
And Moses said unto Jehovah () = indignation because the Divine was not with them...

For Moses had been foreseen by the Lord to be over the Israelitish people, (as) is evident from the fact that he was brought up in the court of king Pharaoh, where there were dominions; and hence he derived a spirit of pre-eminence over others; and therefore he was received to be over his people. His quality also was that he could receive speech from the Divine better than others of that nation; for he was not so much in what is external separated from what is internal as was that nation. Signified.

And He said, My faces shall go, and I will cause thee to rest () = that the Divine of the Church, of worship, and of the Word will be there; but with that nation what is external without it... To make Moses rest = the external of the Church, of worship, and of the Word, in which Divine interior things cease...

And Jehovah said unto Moses, This word also which thou hast spoken I will do () = that the Divine will be in the external of the Church, of worship, and of the Word, which is with them. Moses, as the head of that nation, represents (this) external not so separated from what is internal as was the external of them with the nation itself.

Hence it is that it is now said Moses and the people; now, Moses, without the people; and now the people, without Moses; and that when Moses is speaking to Jehovah, he says I and the people; and when Jehovah to Moses, He speaks of Moses alone; or of the people separated from him. Illustrated.
And he said, Cause me I pray to see Thy glory () = the apperception of internal Divine truth in what is external. Moses here represents (that) external not so separated... AC 10576.

And He said, Thou canst not see My faces () = that the Divine interior things of the Church, etc., cannot appear to the Israelitish nation... Because this is said to Moses, and Moses here represents the head of the Israelitish nation.

(Thus) to place Moses in the fissure of the rock () = what is obscure and false of faith, such as is with those who are in externals without an internal; for by Moses is here meant that people... AC 10583. AC 10584.

By Moses (in ) is represented the external of the Church, of worship, and of the Word which receives Divine truth... (This) is evident from the particulars in this chapter; as that Moses ascended into Mount Sinai... and that the people were removed thence; and in what follows Jehovah speaks to Moses... and not to the people... AC 10614.

That Moses represents this external, and not the internal, is also evident from all the particulars... as that Jehovah descended in a cloud... A like external was represented by Moses in the preceding chapter...
And Moses arose in the morning early, and ascended unto Mount Sinai () = a new rise of the revelation of Divine truth.

And Moses hastened, and bent himself to the earth, and adored () = reception then from influx into the external, and worship from humiliation... Moses represents the external of the Church, etc., which receives the internal. AC 10626.
Moses represents the Word; hence by the people in the midst of whom he is (), is signified the Church where the Word is... AC 10636. AC 10637. AC 10638.

In the descending of Moses from Mount Sinai () = the influx of the internal into the external of the Word, of the Church, and of worship... By Moses is represented the external of the Word in which is the internal. AC 10689.

And Moses knew not that the skin of his faces did shine... () = the internal of the Word shining forth in its external without the external perceiving it. Moses represents the external of the Word in which is the internal. AC 10694. AC 10695.
And he put a veil upon his faces () = that the internal of the Church, of worship, and of the Word appeared not to the Israelitish nation; but only the external without the internal.

And in the entering of Moses before Jehovah to speak with Him () = the state of the external when the internal from the Lord inflowed, and it received information. Moses represents the external in which is the internal. AC 10707.
This is signified by the veil before the face of Moses. Explained.
He removed the veil... () = a state of illustration then. Explained.
It is now evident whence came the sparkling of the faces of Moses, and what is the signification of it. AC 10705.
The faces of Moses = the internal things of AC 10706.
Moses and Elias = the historical and the prophetical Word. AE 64:2. AE 594:2. AE 1070:3.
(In the Word in Heaven) instead of Moses, there is the Historical Word.

And they sang the song of Moses the servant of God... () = confession from charity, thus from a life according to the precepts of the Law which is the decalogue... By Moses is meant, in a wide sense, all the Law written in his five books; and, in a confined sense, the Law which is called the decalogue; and as these subserve a man for life, it is said the song of Moses the servant of God; for by a servant in the Word is meant what subserves; here, life.
The reason why by Moses, in a wide sense is meant the Law, is that his five books are called the Law... That everything written in these books is called the Law of Moses, and also Moses. Illustrated.

From these things it is evident that by Moses, in a wide sense, is meant the Word which has been written by him, which is called the Law. That by Moses is meant the Law which is the decalogue, follows thence, and this the more as Moses engraved the tables after he had broken the former ones; and, when he carried them down, his face was radiant; and therefore Moses is portrayed holding the tables in his hands. It is also said in Mark, Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother (); and in Joshua, Joshua wrote a copy of the law of Moses upon the stones of the altar (). This Law was the decalogue.
Hence it was evident to me whence it was that the face of Moses shone. Explained.
Moses seen. WE 3483. See SE 281. SE 464.
Many things could be said about Moses...
(Moses and Elias at the transfiguration were merely personated.)
Concerning the speech of Spirits with Moses and the prophets.
One of these from the Celestial Kingdom spoke with Moses; and therefore the Jews formed the opinion that Jehovah has a white beard.
Their Word was according to the interior sense... and in place of Moses, Aaron, David, there was the Lord.

Moses appears to the Jews when they do anything evil, with a rod in his hand, and terrifies and admonishes them. A certain Angel in Heaven appears in such a form, and they persuade themselves that it is Moses. LJPost 249. LJPost 312.
a. The Mohammedans acknowledge Moses as a great prophet; but less than the Lord; but they no longer think about Moses.

Concerning Moses, who has been seen. - The Jews asked the Lord that Moses might be shown them, who was therefore seen. He was then below in his own place where the Ancients are, in a quiet state. He came to me also, and I spoke with him. He was a serious man. He said that he seemed to himself to be a man of about fifty years of age, although in the world he had been 120 years old; and that he has with him his five books, and also the ancient Word. I asked him about the Book of Jasher. He said that he has seen it, and told me that that Word is still with the Ancients of his time, and is read. Also that he knows about the following Word which exists at this day, but does not read it. I recounted some things from those which he had written concerning some things in the five books, and he recognized all things, as if they were present to him.
Moses, here () represented that nation, such as it is as to the understanding of the Word...
Because Moses represented the Law, by which is meant Divine truth.
The chief of them represented the Lord as to the Word itself from which is the doctrine of Divine truth; as Moses, Elijah...
As Moses represented the Lord as to the Law, that is, as to the Word... AE 727:11.
The body of Moses. (See Michael.)
They sang the song of Moses the servant of God... = the acknowledgement and confession of the precepts which are in the Word... of the Old Testament.
That Moses = the Word of the Old Testament. Illustrated.
As Moses represented the Law...
As Moses represented the Lord as to the Law or Word...
As by Moses was represented the Lord as to the historical Word...
